title: Khalsa scatters and Sukha Singh directs the retreat

blocks.text: The Khalsa then declared that they must scatter themselves in all the directions and later reassemble in the Majha region to renew the struggle. The decision acknowledged that the present battlefield could no longer be held, but it also turned dispersal into an organized plan for survival and future resistance.

Sukha Singh counseled the Singhs on how to carry out the retreat, telling those on foot to keep climbing while mounted men guarded them from below. He tried to preserve some order in the breakup so the weakest parties would not be abandoned immediately under Mughal pressure.

Even with that guidance, the separation was painful and chaotic, as comrades and families were torn apart in the confusion. The movement away from the hills thus became both a military dispersal and an emotional sundering for a community already battered by hunger, pursuit, and loss.
